concerns.text: Tasks T012a and T012b (data download) are listed in Phase 3 (User Story 1) but are functionally foundational prerequisites for T013 (preprocessing), T014 (MMD), and T016 (evaluation). The spec requires data to exist before any processing can occur. These tasks must be moved to Phase 2 (Foundational) to satisfy the 'Producer before Consumer' dependency rule. Currently, the plan implies preprocessing can happen without the raw data artifact being produced first.

Task T016 (load ground truth, verify source independence) is placed in Phase 3 but depends on the artifact produced by T012b (`ground_truth_events.csv`). Since T012b is currently listed after T016 in the logical flow of the phase (or at least not explicitly before it as a hard dependency), this creates a consumer-before-producer violation. T016 must explicitly follow T012b.

Task T026b (cross-comparison t-test) depends on the output of T026a (baseline delays) and T017 (MMD delays). While T026a is listed before T026b, T026a depends on T025 (`baselines.csv`). T025 is listed *after* T026a in the text flow (T025 is the last item in Implementation for US2, T026a is before it). This is a semantic ordering violation: T026a cannot compute delays from a file (T025) that hasn't been generated yet. T025 must precede T026a.

Task T032 (aggregate metrics) and T033 (update report) depend on the output of T029 and T030 (sensitivity grid execution). T031 is marked as 'Execute sensitivity grid', but T032 and T033 are listed *after* T031. However, T032 implies aggregating results from T029/T030. The dependency chain is T029/T030 -> T031 -> T032 -> T033. The current listing order is acceptable, but T032's description 'Aggregate metrics for all configurations' implies it consumes the output of T031. Ensure T031 is strictly marked as a prerequisite for T032 in the execution logic, as T032 cannot run without the `sensitivity.csv` generated by T031.

Tasks T010 and T011 (tests) are marked [P] (parallel-safe) and placed before implementation tasks T012a-T018. While TDD is a valid strategy, the description for T011 states 'Execution depends on code existing'. If T011 is a true integration test running the full pipeline, it cannot run in parallel with the implementation of T012a-T018 if those tasks are the ones creating the code. If T011 is intended to be written first (TDD) and then fail, the [P] tag is misleading because the *execution* of the test is blocked by the implementation tasks. Clarify if [P] applies to 'writing' only or if the test can actually run in parallel (which it cannot if code is missing).
